description.p: Greenhouse is a torrent client that looks good and keeps everything a click or a keystroke away. Progress is drawn as the row itself, so a list of torrents reads at a glance: download is always teal, upload always amber.

Tracker packs are saved lists of trackers that are attached to every new torrent and magnet link, with no pasting. Push a pack onto torrents you already have, or keep it current from a source URL. Private torrents are only ever announced to the trackers they came with.

ul.li: Paste a magnet link into the search bar, drop a .torrent file, or watch a folder
Follow RSS and Atom feeds, with filters and one copy of each episode
Choose files before downloading and play them while they download
Queue, seeding limits by ratio or time, and speed limits that apply at once
Blocklists, UPnP, and binding traffic to one network interface
A tray menu with live speeds, and notifications when downloads finish
Full keyboard control, a night and a day theme, and six accents

Editing the trackers of one torrent

description.p: Long torrent names with no spaces now wrap in notifications instead of running off the edge.

Private torrents keep their own trackers, the tray menu shows speeds and can pause or resume everything, feeds can filter by pattern and take one copy of each episode, and opening a torrent's folder works again.
The details panel no longer covers the list on narrow windows, and Greenhouse holds fewer connections on systems that allow few open files.
Fixes freezing when started from the dock with many active torrents, and the details panel on narrow windows.
